citations.quote:
Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra. Let $\kappa:\mathfrak g\times\mathfrak g\to\mathbb R$ be a symmetric bilinear form that is invariant, meaning
$$\kappa([U,V],W)=\kappa(U,[V,W])\qquad(U,V,W\in\mathfrak g).$$
No nondegeneracy, positivity, simplicity, or compactness assumption is imposed. Put $S^1=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ and $\mathcal L\mathfrak g=C^\infty(S^1,\mathfrak g)$, with pointwise bracket $[X,Y](\theta)=[X(\theta),Y(\theta)]_{\mathfrak g}$. For $Y\in\mathcal L\mathfrak g$, write $Y'=\partial_\theta Y$ in the indicated periodic coordinate.

A Lie-algebra $2$-cocycle for the trivial scalar action is an alternating bilinear map $\omega:\mathcal L\mathfrak g\times\mathcal L\mathfrak g\to\mathbb R$ satisfying
$$\omega([X,Y],Z)+\omega([Y,Z],X)+\omega([Z,X],Y)=0.$$
Define the candidate current cocycle and its candidate central-term bracket by
$$\omega(X,Y)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\kappa(X(\theta),Y'(\theta))\,d\theta,\qquad \widehat{\mathcal L\mathfrak g}=\mathcal L\mathfrak g\oplus\mathbb R,$$
$$[(X,a),(Y,b)]=([X,Y],\omega(X,Y)).$$
The real coordinates $a,b$ are central coordinates and do not enter the right-hand side. A one-dimensional central extension means a short exact sequence of Lie algebras $0\to\mathbb R\to\widehat{\mathcal L\mathfrak g}\to\mathcal L\mathfrak g\to0$ whose kernel is central. The proposition on this page verifies that the displayed operation has this Lie-algebra structure. The normalization is fixed as written; no integer level, integration to a loop group, or representation-theoretic existence or unitarity follows from this definition.

derivations.claim:
Bilinearity of $\kappa$ and differentiation makes $\omega$ bilinear. By symmetry and the product rule,
$$\omega(X,Y)+\omega(Y,X)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\bigl(\kappa(X,Y')+\kappa(X',Y)\bigr)\,d\theta=\frac1{2\pi}\bigl[\kappa(X,Y)\bigr]_{0}^{2\pi}=0.$$
The endpoint values agree because $X$ and $Y$ are smooth maps on $S^1$, so $\omega$ is skew-symmetric; over $\mathbb R$, this implies $\omega(X,X)=0$.

Invariance and symmetry give
$$\kappa([X,Y],Z')=\kappa(X,[Y,Z']),\quad \kappa([Y,Z],X')=\kappa(X',[Y,Z]),\quad \kappa([Z,X],Y')=\kappa(X,[Y',Z]).$$
The product rule and $[Y,Z]'=[Y',Z]+[Y,Z']$ therefore yield
$$\kappa([X,Y],Z')+\kappa([Y,Z],X')+\kappa([Z,X],Y')=\partial_\theta\kappa(X,[Y,Z]).$$
Integrating over one period makes the right-hand side zero. By the definition of $\omega$, this is the required cyclic cocycle identity.

The displayed operation is bilinear and skew-symmetric by the pointwise Lie bracket and step 1.1. The vector component of its Jacobi sum is the pointwise Jacobi sum in $\mathfrak g$, hence vanishes at every $\theta$. Its real component is the cyclic sum in step 1.2, hence also vanishes. Thus the operation satisfies Jacobi and is a Lie bracket.

The maps $i(a)=(0,a)$ and $p(X,a)=X$ are Lie-algebra homomorphisms: the bracket of any two elements in $\operatorname{im}i$ is zero, and $p([(X,a),(Y,b)])=[X,Y]$. The projection is surjective because $p(X,0)=X$, and $\ker p=\{(0,a):a\in\mathbb R\}=\operatorname{im}i$. Moreover $[(0,a),(Y,b)]=(0,\omega(0,Y))=(0,0)$ by bilinearity of $\omega$, so the kernel is central. This proves the asserted central extension.

boundaries.evidence: If g is the zero Lie algebra, then every loop, cocycle value, and bracket component is zero; the exact sequence reduces to 0 → R → R → 0 → 0 in steps 2.1–3.1.
For X=Y=Z=0 every integrand and every bracket in steps 1.1–3.1 vanishes.
For constant loops X and Y, Y′=0 so ω(X,Y)=0; the extension restricts to the ordinary constant-loop bracket by the definition and step 3.1.
If κ is degenerate, including κ=0, the proof uses only symmetry and invariance; for κ=0 the cocycle is zero and steps 2.1–3.1 still give the direct central extension.
The only endpoint contribution is [κ(X,Y)]₀²π in step 1.1, and periodicity makes it exactly zero.

boundaries.reason: The proof integrates explicit smooth loops over one compact period and uses no choice principle.
The proposition asserts a cocycle identity and central extension, not an equivalence.
The proposition asserts a cocycle identity and central extension, not an equivalence.

finite_checks.calculation: For X(θ)=U and Y(θ)=V constant, Y′=0 and ω(X,Y)=0.
finite_checks.disposition: Direct normalization check of the definition and step 1.1.

finite_checks.calculation: For an abelian one-dimensional g with κ(U,V)=c, X(θ)=U sin θ and Y(θ)=V cos θ give ω(X,Y)=−c/2 and ω(Y,X)=c/2; their sum is zero.
finite_checks.disposition: Finite integral check of step 1.1 with the stated 1/(2π) normalization.

citations.quote:
Fix a four-dimensional model with a finite-dimensional gauge Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a chosen basis $\{t^a\}$, and a finite family of left-handed Weyl matter fields indexed by $i$. A left-handed Weyl species here means a massless two-component spinor field whose gauge transformation is given by a finite-dimensional complex representation $\rho_i:\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C}\to\operatorname{End}(V_i)$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V_i$. Write $T^a_{R_i}=\rho_i(t^a)$ for its generator matrices, and define the matrix anticommutator by $\{A,B\}=AB+BA$. The perturbative cubic gauge coefficient interface is
$$d^{abc}=\sum_i\operatorname{tr}_{V_i}\!\left(T^a_{R_i}\{T^b_{R_i},T^c_{R_i}\}\right).$$
The trace and generator normalization are fixed by the chosen model convention. In particular, no factor $1/2$ is included in the anticommutator. If symmetrization is defined by $T^{(b}T^{c)}=(T^bT^c+T^cT^b)/2$, then our $d^{abc}$ is exactly twice $\sum_i\operatorname{tr}_{V_i}(T^a_{R_i}T^{(b}_{R_i}T^{c)}_{R_i})$. Cancellation means vanishing in the same declared convention.

If the model is coupled to a background spacetime connection with curvature two-form $\mathcal R$, record mixed gauge-gravitational anomaly data separately from $d^{abc}$. For a gauge generator $t^a$, its representation trace coefficient is
$$\ell^a=\sum_i\operatorname{tr}_{V_i}(T^a_{R_i});$$
for a $U(1)$ factor whose generator acts on species $i$ by its charge $q_i$, this is $\ell=\sum_iq_i$. In the usual six-form index-polynomial description the mixed term is proportional, with convention-dependent constants, to $\ell^a F^a\wedge\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal R\wedge\mathcal R)$; the gauge-curvature and spacetime-curvature conventions must be stated when using it. This interface records the coefficient data and does not assert that a regulated Ward anomaly has this form.

A local consistent anomaly is an infinitesimal gauge variation of a regulated effective action whose local density obeys the gauge-algebra consistency condition. In the local BRST notation used here, its four-dimensional representative is a compactly supported local horizontal four-form $a_4$ of ghost number one in a specified $s,d_H$-stable subcomplex $\mathcal K^{r,p}$ of finite-jet local forms on $\mathbb R^4$. The relative class is
$$[a_4]_{s|d_H}\in H^{1,4}(s|d_H;\mathcal K):=\frac{\{a_4\in\mathcal K^{1,4}:s a_4+d_Ha_3=0\text{ for some }a_3\in\mathcal K^{2,3}\}}{\{s b_4+d_Hc_3:b_4\in\mathcal K^{0,4},\ c_3\in\mathcal K^{1,3}\}}.$$
Here $s$ is the odd nilpotent local BRST differential and $d_H$ is the horizontal exterior derivative on spacetime local forms. A descent class means the relative class of the ghost-number-one four-form obtained by descending a specified invariant six-form polynomial; the descent and its local hypotheses must be stated.

The available local Wess–Zumino obstruction interface is conditional. Its exact upstream statement assumes the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice, an admissible flat scalar free datum and local scalar polynomial class under the scalar formal time-ordering result, and a time-ordering scheme satisfying that result. It further assumes an odd formal ghost-number-one Ward operator $\mathcal W_\hbar=s+O(\hbar)$ with $\mathcal W_\hbar^2=0$, a first breaking at formal order $n\ge1$ represented by a compactly supported local $a_4\in\mathcal K^{1,4}$, an $s,d_H$-stable subcomplex $\mathcal K$, and $\mathcal K^{0,4}$ equal to the admissible local counterterm densities. Under those hypotheses the upstream proposition states that $s a_4$ is $d_H$-exact and that a local counterterm cancels the order-$n$ breaking exactly when $[a_4]_{s|d_H}=0$. This is only a conditional local consistency result: it does not prove locality of a physical anomaly, a quantum action principle, or any identification between $d^{abc}$ and a descent representative.

Accordingly, an anomaly-cancellation claim using $d^{abc}$ must state the regulator and renormalization construction, prove the identification of its local consistent anomaly with the descent class of the declared coefficient tensor, specify the mixed gauge-gravitational coefficients separately, and state the loop-order hypotheses or all-orders theorem being used. A global anomaly is a possible failure under a gauge transformation outside the identity component of the full gauge-transformation group; it requires its own global group, bundle, and spacetime data and is not determined by the infinitesimal local tensor $d^{abc}$. Vanishing $d^{abc}$ alone is not defined here to establish a nonperturbative gauge theory or cancellation of global anomalies.

derivations.claim: In one dimension the trace of a scalar is that scalar, and $\{q,q\}=2q^2$, $\{-q,-q\}=2q^2$. Therefore the two contributions to the cubic coefficient sum to $q(2q^2)+(-q)(2q^2)=2(q^3+(-q)^3)=0$.

The linear trace coefficient is $q+(-q)=0$. Thus both the Abelian cubic coefficient and the separately tracked mixed linear coefficient vanish by direct arithmetic. This calculation asserts no descent identification, loop theorem, global-anomaly conclusion, or nonperturbative existence claim.
